exact_statement: For every real epsilon>0, prove that there exists A subset N of natural density greater than 1-epsilon such that for all finite subsets S,T subset A, equality prod(S)=prod(T) implies |S|=|T|; and prove finite sets A_N subset {1,...,N} with |A_N|=(1-o(1))N and the same Finset product-cardinality property. Elements may not repeat within either product.
scope_notes: Variant lock: products are Finset products. Within each side every integer is used at most once. The two sides may overlap, and common factors may then be cancelled. No multiset or repeated-factor argument is admissible.

The repetitions-allowed version is excluded. In that stronger variant arbitrary integer coefficients occur in prime-exponent relations and a totally additive function can be invoked; that is a variant mismatch here, where coefficients after cancellation lie only in {-1,0,1}.

Write v(n)=(nu_p(n))_p. The exact property is: every finitely supported coefficient vector c in {-1,0,1} with support in A and sum_n c_n v(n)=0 must satisfy sum_n c_n=0. Finite optimum values without an all-N theorem or completeness reduction are non-success.
The empty Finset has product one, so 1 cannot belong to an admissible set. Likewise 0 cannot occur in any positive-density admissible set; the density assertions are unaffected by deleting {0,1}.

The infinite assertion implies the finite assertion by intersection with [1,N]. The converse is not automatic because independently optimized finite sets need not be nested and multiplicative relations can cross concatenated blocks.

For the infinite part, natural density means one limiting density delta exists and delta>1-epsilon. Upper density, logarithmic density, density along a subsequence, or a different A_N for each cutoff does not suffice.
For the finite part, [N] means {1,...,N}; one must construct A_N with |A_N|/N tending to one and the full Finset product-cardinality property for every N (modifying finitely many N is harmless).

A proof of only the known density-1/e Selfridge construction, a bounded-factor-length version, a bounded-prime-support version, a SAT optimum through fixed N, or a conditional admission lemma does not close either requested density-one statement.
Public search for an exact solution is prohibited. The frozen local Lean formalization and ordinary named background are permitted sources.

variant_lock.allowed: finite subsets / Finsets of distinct integers on each side
variant_lock.forbidden: multisets, repeated use of an element on one side, or importing the totally additive-function obstruction for the repetitions-allowed problem

exact_subproblems.infinite: For every epsilon>0, construct A subset N with natural density delta>1-epsilon and the distinct-factor product-cardinality property.
exact_subproblems.finite: Construct A_N subset [N] with |A_N|=(1-o(1))N and the same property.
exact_subproblems.one_way_interface: The infinite construction implies the finite result by truncation.
